newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks joint French bid for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: France seeks joint French bid for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: The French government is urging rivals Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere to bury the hatchet and bid jointly for Thomson-CSF to create a French defence electronics giant with global aspirations.
It also made clear Thursday that it was looking for future defence industry partners in Europe, but that bids that would leave the company in non-French hands would not be welcome.

"The government isn't imposing a marriage on them (Alcatel and Lagardere) but this is what it has asked the chairmen of these companies to do," said a government official, confirming reports that Prime Minister Alain Juppe was looking for a joint offer.
Alcatel and Lagardere have been at loggerheads since the government failed last year in its first attempt to privatise Thomson-CSF's parent -- the Thomson SA group .
"We need to reinforce the defence electronics industry ...especially when you consider the huge concentration taking place across the Atlantic," the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
He said the government planned to use the privatisation of its 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF initially as an opportunity to group together the main French defence players.
"During this first phase, the French companies can indicate who their allies are within the European industry," he said. But he said the plan was to forge European links at a later stage.
The French government is not open, he said, to a purely foreign offer, even from a European company such as Britain's GEC Plc which has ties to both Lagardere and Alcatel.

A spokesman for Alcatel declined to comment on the possibility of a joint bid but recalled Chairman Serge Tchuruk's recent remarks that it would be unwise to have too many "contradictory interests" represented on Thomson-CSF's board.
